newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down across the board on Wednesday on a powerful technical correction after sharp rises on Tuesday, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract plunged to 16.2 percent from 30 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 3.99 million lots from 10.49 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
All the repo rates surged on Tuesday due to new domestic A share issues and strong performances on the A share markets.
"A powerful technical correction on the repo market was expected," said a trader. "The rises yesterday were too sharp."
Traders said that after the correction, repo rates were likely to move around the current level for the coming few days.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up across the board on Wednesday on renewed market talk that the central bank would soon cut bank interest rates, traders said. Officials have declined to comment.
The most active three-year bond maturing in August 1999 rose to 104.94 yuan from 104.82 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell to 1.05 million lots from 1.14 million lots.
The rises were also attributed to a technical correction on the domestic A share markets, which drove some liquidity back to the T-bill spot market, traders said.
Traders said market sentiment was good because of the high yields of existing contracts. They said prices would continue to rise in the near term, barring any major negative news.
